Subject: ACME — RAG eval recap & recommended next steps

Hi Jill — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Goals we heard: improve grounding/attribution on knowledge-base answers, get <1s median token latency for short queries, and reduce hallucination rate on policy FAQs to <2%.
2) Current constraints: ACME wants private VPC deployment (ok), data residency US, and SSO.
3) Initial model fit recommendations (based on your sample dataset + call):
   - Start with an Llama 2 70B quantized variant for the generator (good tradeoff for long-form grounding quality).
   - Use a cross-encoder reranker (DistilCross-encoder tuned on your QA pairs) for top-10 -> top-3 filtering before generation.
   - Retrieval: dense embeddings (text-embedding-ada style baseline) with Faiss HNSW; aggressive chunking (max 1,200 tokens) and BM25 hybrid for recall-sensitive queries.

Deliverables we’ll share by Thursday: a short eval report (precision/recall/grounding metrics), the prompt sets we used, and a recording of the demo run. I attached the preliminary eval report and prompt CSV to this thread.

Next steps: 
- I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk the eval results and collect prioritization — proposed slots: Thu 10:00am or Fri 2:00pm PT. Which works best?
- Marcus will provide the recommended reranker configs and estimated cost delta for dedicated capacity.

Thanks — I’ll action items on our side once you confirm the time.

—

2) On the reranker: are you recommending a cross-encoder for production or just for offline eval? We’re concerned about latency if the cross-encoder is in the critical path.
3) Can you include grounding metrics we can show to our security team (precision@1 for grounded responses, % of responses with source links)?

Great, Thu 10:00am PT booked — calendar invite sent. Answers inline below and attaching a brief appendix for the security team: 

1) Model choice: for short, high-precision prompts we still recommend the 70B generator initially because it produced the best grounding precision in your QA eval (precision@1 = 0.92 on sample set). Downsizing to a 13B quantized generator reduced hallucination but also lowered helpfulness in multi-step answers — we can trial a 13B fallback in the routing policy after baseline.

2) Reranker placement: recommended pattern is cross-encoder during candidate re-ranking (top-10 dense retrieval -> cross-encoder -> top-3). To control latency in production, we suggest: 
   - Deploy cross-encoder on dedicated CPU/GPU pool with batching and async pre-rerank for common queries, or
   - Use a distilled cross-encoder for the critical path (approx 2–3x faster) and keep the larger cross-encoder for offline periodic re-tuning.
Estimated latency impact (P95): +60–120ms if using distilled cross-encoder in-path; +200–350ms for full cross-encoder depending on batch. We’ll include exact numbers and capacity estimates in Marcus’s note.

3) Grounding/security metrics: included in the attached eval PDF and appendix — precision@1, grounding-coverage (responses with >=1 source link), and attribution-consistency (source overlap vs. expected doc). We also have a short SOC 2 evidence checklist for retrieval logs and audit traceability.

Attachments: redwood-eval-report.pdf, acme-rag-prompt-sets.csv, security-appendix.pdf

Looking forward to the call.

—
Marissa

Subject: Re: ACME — RAG eval recap & recommended next steps

Hi Jill — adding the reranker/cost details as promised. Quick summary: 

- Reranker options we tested: DistilCross-encoder (6B distilled), FullCross-encoder (base 220M cross-encoder finetuned). DistilCross gave 0.89 precision@1, FullCross 0.92 on your eval set.
- Deployment patterns: 
  * DistilCross in-path: supports ~600 qps on a single dedicated GPU with P95 ~120ms + generator time.
  * FullCross isolated async re-rank: offers best quality, but expect P95 +250–350ms depending on batch.
- Cost delta: ~ +18–28% on token/unit costs for dedicated capacity if you run an in-path DistilCross, and +30–45% if you run FullCross high-availability in-path. Exact numbers linked in the drive doc.

Recommended immediate plan for PoC: 
1) Start with DistilCross in-path + Llama2-70B quantized generator. This gives a strong balance of grounding quality and latency.
2) Add hybrid retrieval (dense + BM25) to improve recall for short token queries.
3) Enable detailed retrieval logging and grounding coverage metric so security can validate. We’ll provide a short playbook for retention & access controls for logs.

I uploaded a short cost worksheet and the reranker config to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExampleLinkEval

If procurement needs an estimate for a reserved capacity commitment we can spin a draft SOW and numbers — ping me and I’ll get the finance team involved.
